artworks.title: The Dionysus Cup
artworks.description: Exekias' Munich kylix: Dionysus reclines in a vine-masted ship among dolphins — the Homeric Hymn's Tyrrhenian pirate metamorphosis, the voyage on which Acoetes alone recognizes the god. Staatliche Antikensammlungen.

artworks.title: Dionysus and the Tyrrhenian Pirates (Choragic Monument of Lysicrates)
artworks.artist: James Stuart & Nicholas Revett (after the Athenian reliefs)
artworks.description: Stuart and Revett's engraving of the Lysicrates monument frieze: Dionysus' capture and the pirates' dolphin doom — Acoetes' shipmates punished while the believing pilot is spared in Ovid's telling.

artworks.title: Tyrrhenian Pirates into Dolphins (Micali Painter hydria)
artworks.description: Etruscan black-figure hydria: Dionysus' captors mid-metamorphosis into dolphins — the pirate crew of the Bacchic voyage whose sole pious helmsman, in Ovid, is Acoetes.

popCulture.title: Acoetes (Bacchic myth)
popCulture.description: Tyrrhenian pilot who alone recognizes Dionysus among the pirates — spared when his shipmates become dolphins. Not the Trojan Acoetes of the Aeneid nor the father of Laocoön.

popCulture.title: Metamorphoses (Bacchus and the Tyrrhenian sailors)
popCulture.creator: Ovid
popCulture.description: Ovid's Acoetes narrates the pirate voyage to Pentheus (Met. 3) — the helmsman's testimony as the god's living witness.

popCulture.title: Homeric Hymns
popCulture.description: The archaic hymn corpus that tells the Tyrrhenian seizure of Dionysus — the pirate episode Acoetes later voices in Ovid.
